# Combat > Damage and Healing

*[Rules Glossary](../../index.md)*

Taking damage, damage types and defenses, healing, and dropping to 0 Hit Points.

## Entries

- [Bloodied](Bloodied.md): A creature is Bloodied while it has half its Hit Points or fewer remaining.
- [Damage](Damage.md): Damage represents harm that causes a creature or an object to lose Hit Points.
- [Damage Roll](Damage-Roll.md): A damage roll is a die roll, adjusted by any applicable modifiers, that deals damage to a target.
- [Damage Threshold](Damage-Threshold.md): A creature or an object that has a damage threshold has Immunity to all damage unless it takes an amount of damage from a single attack or effect equal to or greater than its damage threshold, in w...
- [Damage Types](Damage-Types.md): Attacks and other harmful effects deal different types of damage.
- [Dead](Dead.md): A dead creature has no Hit Points and can't regain them unless it is first revived by magic such as the Raise Dead or Revivify spell.
- [Death Saving Throw](Death-Saving-Throw.md): A player character must make a Death Saving Throw (also called a Death Save) if they start their turn with 0 Hit Points.
- [Healing](Healing.md): Healing is how you regain Hit Points.
- [Immunity](Immunity.md): If you have Immunity to a damage type or a condition, it doesn't affect you in any way.
- [Knocking Out a Creature](Knocking-Out-a-Creature.md): When you would reduce a creature to 0 Hit Points with a melee attack, you can instead reduce the creature to 1 Hit Point.
- [Resistance](Resistance.md): If you have Resistance to a damage type, damage of that type is halved against you (round down).
- [Stable](Stable.md): A creature is Stable if it has 0 Hit Points but isn't required to make Death Saving Throws.
- [Vulnerability](Vulnerability.md): If you have Vulnerability to a damage type, damage of that type is doubled against you.
